items.title: Bill Berry and Buster Cooper interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: And it had within that band it had Clifford Brown, Art Farmer and Quincy Jones and like big names you know.

ctx.x: Tell us some of the early bands that you played with, how you got your start professionally.

Well I started with my cousin’s big band, I mean, but first, I was born and raised in St. Petersburg, Florida. And then I went to high school, you know, the same thing, the teacher in the high school band, the teacher and stuff like that. And my cousin had a 16- piece band you know. So naturally blood is thicker than water so he let me ease in there some kind of way, you know. So after I finished high school like in St. Petersburg, I went to New York you know. And my first big band was Lionel Hampton’s band you…
but we weren’t making no money but the band sure was swinging. You understand what I’m saying?

items.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: some of these guys were there like Quincy Jones and Buster Cooper and a couple others. We played some

ctx.x: When we got back to LA with the McShann band, that’s when things really started happening. That’s when I started working with Dexter and Wardell, Gerald Wilson, Benny Carter, people like that. But it wasn’t enough for a livelihood, so I was working at the LA County General Hospital as an x-ray clerk in the daytime ‘cause I never really felt like hustling or hitting on people, “let me have five,” or whatever. I worked there, and in the meantime, I was working with these other people, whoever called me for a job, I…
When did you arrive back there with McShann and when did you leave?
